case_prompt: A 21-year-old man was admitted with a 1-week history of swelling and pain in both knees, both ankles, the right shoulder, and the right wrist, accompanied by fever. Physical examination revealed redness, swelling, and a subcutaneous hematoma over the right ankle with increased local skin temperature. He reported an antecedent “cold” and had experienced watery diarrhea 3 days before the onset of joint symptoms. Laboratory tests showed a leukocyte count of 11.78 × 10^9/L (neutrophils 82.9%), platelet count of 384 × 10^9/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 77 mm/h, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein of 176.49 mg/L, uric acid of 250.5 µmol/L, activated partial thromboplastin time of 44.60 s, fibrinogen of 6.74 g/L, D-dimer of 10.67 µg/mL, and factor VIII activity of 203.7%. Aspiration of the right ankle yielded bloody fluid with numerous leukocytes and red blood cells. Debridement of an ulcerated, necrotic subcutaneous hematoma was performed and cultures of joint fluid and wound secretions were negative. Magnetic resonance imaging of the right ankle suggested inflammatory arthritis. Tests for rheumatic factor, antinuclear antibodies, HLA-B27, stool cultures, and other infectious agents were negative. On hospital day 3, he developed severe left perianal pain with localized skin redness and swelling, and a diagnosis of perianal abscess was made.

diagnostic_reasoning: 1. Exclusion of septic or tuberculous arthritis — “patients with joint pain accompanied by fever are easily misdiagnosed as septic arthritis or tuberculous arthritis, which can be excluded according to the history, signs, and results of joint fluid culture.” 2. Support for reactive arthritis — “we considered ReA.”

selection.screen_reason: Asymmetric oligo/polyarthritis after a cold and diarrhoea with sterile joint fluid and negative serologies supports reactive arthritis.
selection.second_look_note: An antecedent cold and watery diarrhea three days before polyarthritis are the decisive history clues, with sterile joint fluid and negative serologies.
